title: Qargo Coffee: what the FTC alleged about license labels
description: A bounded historical case connects the actual 2024 complaint to reported settlement status, without treating a label as legal clearance.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The specific historical record
paragraphs: Real case. In its complaint filed 16 October 2024 in the Southern District of Florida, the FTC alleged that Qargo Coffee’s California offering used “distributorship” and affiliated-license language while operating as a franchise. Paragraphs 26–35 describe the brand, fees, controls and support facts on which the FTC relied. These are allegations in a complaint, not findings from a contested trial.

sections.heading: Reported outcome and the remaining limit
paragraphs: The FTC’s December 2024 litigation report records entry of a stipulated order on 17 October 2024. Its later report to Congress covering fiscal 2025 lists the Qargo matter’s outcome as Full Settlement. Those official records support a historical settlement account; they do not prove collection, current compliance, or that no other disputes exist.

sections.heading: Why this page does not recite final remedy terms
paragraphs: The FTC case index still uses a Pending label and links the filed proposed order. The actual signed entered order was not obtained in this batch. This page therefore does not describe final monetary, rescission or noncompete terms. A proposed document is not silently substituted for the final order, and stale index metadata is not treated as proof that settlement never occurred.

sections.heading: The preparation decision for a management team
paragraphs: A brand owner can keep the useful lesson narrow: record what the partner actually receives, pays and must do before selecting a contract label. Separate trademark-quality protections from broader operating controls, and analyse federal definitions/exemptions and state requirements independently. The shared federal classification guide explains today’s framework; this historical complaint is not a transaction-specific verdict.

sections.heading: Reusable evidence checklist
paragraphs: Output: a relationship factsheet assigned to the expansion lead before prospective rights are marketed.
bullets: Map brand rights, payment recipients and timing.
Retain contract drafts, presentations and spoken sales promises.
Describe training, operational assistance, mandatory systems and enforcement rights.
Identify offer, party and proposed-operation locations.
Record who will analyse the federal and state questions and the factual assumptions that need confirmation.
Keep final-order remedies and present docket status unresolved until their actual evidence is read.

practicalOutput: Relationship factsheet with a bounded historical case reference
limitations: Actual signed final-order terms remain unreviewed and are not stated.
No present conduct, money-recovery or complete current-docket finding is made.
label: Real case — allegations, admissions and historical procedural scope are distinguished

title: Alacrity: a janitorial payroll failure documented in a consent judgment
description: A real 2025 service-business order links worker classification, time records and management responsibility.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Read the admissions and the dates separately
paragraphs: Real case. The official 17-page consent judgment in Alacrity Employment Services / Hawaii Care and Cleaning bears a judicial date of 14 January 2025 and a filing stamp of 15 January 2025 in the District of Hawaii, case 1:24-cv-00567. This was a consent resolution. Unlike settlements that disclaim liability, its paragraph I.Q expressly records admissions of willful violations concerning misclassification, overtime and time/payroll records during the stated 2021–2024 period.

sections.heading: What the identified order required
paragraphs: The judgment states $3,850,000, comprising $1,900,000 back wages, $1,900,000 liquidated damages and $50,000 civil money penalties. Its operative provisions address worker reclassification, accurate records, payroll practices, nonretaliation and supervisor training. These are this case’s terms, not an automatic damages formula for every service business.

sections.heading: A separate entity did not settle the operating facts
paragraphs: The order describes the relationship between the labour-supplying operation and the cleaning company. For an expanding brand, the useful question is who actually directs schedules, sets pay, keeps time and controls working conditions. A staffing, contractor or franchise label cannot replace a fact-specific employment analysis.

sections.heading: Build a payroll-control map
paragraphs: Original preparation exercise: trace one job from customer schedule to worker assignment, time capture, corrections, travel, breaks, pay calculation and approval. Name the operating employer and each person who can change a record. Retain the reason and confirmation for a correction. A signed timesheet is evidence to examine, not a reason to ignore contradictory operational records.

sections.heading: Reusable evidence checklist
paragraphs: Output: a payroll responsibility and evidence map owned by the operating and payroll leads.
bullets: Record the actual worker relationship and responsibilities.
Show who sets schedules, rates and time-record corrections.
Map travel and breaks using applicable law and actual facts.
Assign record retention, review and escalation.
Give managers a way to report payroll problems without retaliation.
Do not describe ordered money as collected: payment performance and later docket developments were not verified.

limitations: Historical identified order, not a full present docket search or recovery finding.
An apparent payment-date/installment-count inconsistency in the source remains unresolved; no payment schedule is reproduced.
label: Real case — allegations, admissions and historical procedural scope are distinguished

title: Restaurant expansion starts with the actual local food process
description: Separate the FDA model code, adopted rules and address-dependent opening evidence.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The federal model is not your local permission
paragraphs: FDA identifies its 2026 Food Code as the latest model edition. The agency explains that regulators use the model to develop or update their own retail and food-service rules. Publication of a model is different from adoption in your state, county, city, tribal or territorial jurisdiction. Do not describe the 2026 edition as automatically governing every restaurant.

sections.heading: Define the proposed operation
paragraphs: Record menu, preparation steps, storage, service format and whether food is made on site, centrally prepared or imported. A takeaway counter, full kitchen, mobile unit and commissary can create different processes. Record the actual address and use before the team relies on a permit route.

sections.heading: Make the opening sequence explicit
paragraphs: Ask the local food authority and building/use authority for the actual review path and evidence. Assign menu/process review, plans, equipment, water/waste, inspection and staff-training questions. Landlord approval and an equipment supplier’s statement are different evidence from an authority’s permission.

sections.heading: Fictional management decision
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European brand plans a compact kitchen using equipment specified for its home market. Before a lease commitment, the operations lead checks whether the proposed menu and equipment fit the actual premises process. Costs and timing stay unknown until sourced; no universal permit delay is assumed.

sections.heading: Prepare one site-opening brief
paragraphs: Output: a food-operation and premises dependency sheet owned by the launch lead.
bullets: Name the actual food and premises authorities.
Record the locally adopted rule/version and unresolved variations.
Map menu, equipment, preparation and storage.
Identify what must precede lease, fit-out, inspection and opening.
Keep operating permission separate from franchise offer/sale analysis.

practicalOutput: Local food-process and premises dependency sheet
limitations: No particular restaurant, jurisdiction, food permit, equipment or inspection approval.

title: Fitness subscriptions need a consent and stop-charge workflow
description: Map the actual seller, Internet checkout and recurring-payment process before a U.S. studio launches.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the transaction the customer experiences
paragraphs: For an Internet transaction using a negative-option feature, 15 U.S.C. § 8403 requires material terms before billing information, express informed consent before charging and simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges. The statute is one relevant federal rule; this guide is not a complete account of state health-club, auto-renewal or cancellation law.

sections.heading: Identify who makes and fulfils the promise
paragraphs: Record the seller, payment-account owner, platform provider and studio operator. Who receives a cancellation, stops the next charge, handles a freeze or transfer and answers a complaint? A brand’s central website can create obligations and operational dependencies for a local operator even where billing runs locally.

sections.heading: Price management and capacity realistically
paragraphs: Test staffing, class capacity, cancellations, cleaning, instructor cover and manager costs before applying a royalty. Record lease and equipment commitments separately from membership cash. A full timetable is not evidence that seats will be sold or that all collected cash is earned immediately.

sections.heading: Fictional launch test
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Southeast Asian studio sells a monthly plan online through a central checkout. The launch team tests the actual screens and a stop-charge request using a test account, including the handoff to the local studio. Record process evidence, not a badge declaring legal compliance.

sections.heading: Prepare the subscription responsibility sheet
paragraphs: Output: a checkout-to-cancellation map owned by customer operations and the payment lead.
bullets: Retain the version of terms shown before billing information.
Record how consent is captured before the charge.
Test the simple stop-charge mechanism and its operator.
Check state health-club, refund and renewal questions separately.
Assign complaints, refunds and service-continuity responsibilities.

practicalOutput: Fitness payment, consent and stop-charge responsibility map
limitations: Scope is Internet negative-option transactions under the cited statute; other rules remain unresolved.

title: A clinical-testing brand needs a laboratory-authorisation workstream
description: Define the actual tests and certificate path before treating a healthcare model as transferable.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The test activity changes the launch sequence
paragraphs: CMS states that CLIA regulates human laboratory testing for health assessment or diagnosis, prevention or treatment of disease. Its requirements vary with test-method complexity. A brand licence, foreign laboratory credential or management team does not by itself settle the U.S. testing permissions.

sections.heading: Separate the operator and professional roles
paragraphs: Record the legal operator, laboratory location, test menu, methods, ordering/reporting process and qualified responsible people. Collect the relevant certificate-path evidence and state laboratory/professional questions. A waived test category is not a general statement that no certificate or other operating duty applies.

sections.heading: Move this ahead of property and partner commitments
paragraphs: A customer-demand exercise is useful, but do not promise the testing service before the operating pathway is resolved. Identify dependencies for the premises, personnel, laboratory director, quality system, equipment and referral arrangements. Payer enrollment and state professional permissions are separate questions.

sections.heading: Fictional capability test
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European diagnostic-services brand proposes a limited U.S. test menu. Its COO first maps each test and who would perform it; the next task is a certificate and state-scope review, not simply finding a master franchise buyer.

sections.heading: Prepare the testing-scope factsheet
paragraphs: Output: a test/menu/operator worksheet owned by the clinical operations lead.
bullets: Name actual tests, purposes and method complexity evidence.
Identify operator, location and responsible qualified personnel.
Record CLIA certificate pathway and unresolved state/professional rules.
Separate testing permission, reimbursement and brand rights.
Keep fees, completion dates and exceptions unresolved until confirmed.

limitations: No clinical guidance, CLIA certificate approval, state authorisation or payer determination.

title: Home-care payroll: distinguish the regulation from enforcement policy
description: A useful plan records the current rule text, agency position and unresolved exposure separately.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Two official sources answer different questions
paragraphs: Current 29 CFR 552.109 states that third-party employers may not claim the companionship minimum-wage/overtime exemption or the live-in overtime exemption described there. DOL’s 25 July 2025 FAB 2025-4 separately directs WHD staff not to apply the 2013 provisions while that policy remains applicable. The bulletin expressly says it does not alter statutory or regulatory requirements or create enforceable rights.

sections.heading: Do not turn enforcement discretion into a payroll saving
paragraphs: The bulletin and current regulation should be recorded together, with their different functions. A proposed rule is not an effective repeal. Final-rule developments, litigation, private claims and state/local law need a current review before costs rely on any exemption. An older public FAQ must not silently replace the later enforcement bulletin.

sections.heading: Specify the service before choosing the model
paragraphs: Separate companionship, personal care, trained nursing and other healthcare tasks. Record actual duties, employer relationships, worker locations, scheduling, travel and supervision. State home-care, health and professional-authorisation requirements remain an independent early workstream; this guide does not identify a universal licence.

sections.heading: Fictional planning decision
paragraphs: Fictional example: a management-run agency proposes two clients per worker per day. The finance lead records hours, travel and alternative wage scenarios without assuming the agency is exempt. A responsible employment reviewer must resolve the applicable treatment before hiring and pricing commitments.

sections.heading: Prepare the law-and-policy decision log
paragraphs: Output: a service/employer/payroll map with source versions and unresolved decisions.
bullets: Identify actual duties and every potential employer.
Record the current regulation and relevant enforcement policy separately.
Check for effective final rules and relevant court developments.
Model pay and travel on supported assumptions; preserve uncertainty.
Assign state licensing, professional and employment review before commitments.

practicalOutput: Home-care payroll and source-conflict decision log
limitations: Agency policy is not repeal, immunity or an individual exemption decision.
State/local and private-enforcement exposure remains unresolved.

title: Home renovation requires a lead-work scope check before promotion
description: Identify building age, actual tasks and certification responsibilities before transferring a home-improvement service.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A task can create obligations before work starts
paragraphs: EPA’s Renovation, Repair and Painting guidance addresses paid renovation disturbing paint in relevant housing and child-occupied facilities built before 1978. It describes firm certification, training, pre-renovation education and work practices, with defined exceptions. EPA also states that firms cannot advertise covered renovation without firm certification.

sections.heading: Describe the actual job
paragraphs: Record building age and use, surfaces, task, affected area and paint evidence. Window replacement, demolition and prohibited practices need particular attention to the actual exception rules. Do not treat a customer’s statement that paint looks new as proof of an exemption.

sections.heading: Separate three authorisations
paragraphs: Brand rights, EPA/state-authorised lead-program responsibilities and state/local contractor or trade permissions are separate. Name the firm undertaking work, appropriately qualified individual and subcontractor interface. Assign evidence before advertising a service or accepting work.

sections.heading: Fictional rollout question
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Southeast Asian home-renovation brand wants one partner to offer repainting and window replacement. The launch team first builds a job-screening and certification process; a simple whole-house price imported from the home market cannot include unverified scope or waste costs.

sections.heading: Prepare the renovation job gate
paragraphs: Output: a building/task/evidence checklist owned by operations.
bullets: Identify property age, use and proposed tasks.
Record the exact basis for any exception.
Assign firm and individual certification evidence.
Check state-authorised lead programs and local trade questions.
Price training, work practices, waste and customer communication using actual scope.

limitations: No job-specific exception, contractor licence or lead-safety approval.

title: HVAC expansion needs an equipment and technician-scope map
description: Match refrigerant, task and certification before promising U.S. repair capacity.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with what the technician will do
paragraphs: EPA’s Section 608 overview identifies certification for technicians maintaining, servicing, repairing or disposing of equipment that could release ozone-depleting refrigerants. Determine the actual equipment, refrigerant and task before assigning a requirement or exception. Do not infer a universal rule for every substitute refrigerant from this short overview.

sections.heading: Separate qualification from a brand training certificate
paragraphs: A brand can teach its diagnostic method without establishing every legal qualification. Record the person’s actual certification category, evidence and scope. State contractor/trade licensing, local permits, recovery equipment and waste responsibilities are independent questions.

sections.heading: Make the response promise fundable
paragraphs: An emergency service promise needs dispatch cover, travel, spare parts, technical escalation, tools and customer communication. Cost the qualified people needed at the first market’s density. A home-country manager cannot automatically replace an appropriately authorised U.S. technician.

sections.heading: Fictional market test
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European HVAC service brand investigates one equipment family in one service corridor. It checks real installed equipment and customer procurement, then identifies the personnel and environmental-work pathway. It does not buy a whole-state territory before proving delivery capacity.

sections.heading: Prepare the technician matrix
paragraphs: Output: an equipment/task/person map owned by the technical lead.
bullets: Record equipment, refrigerant and service/disposal tasks.
Match each person to actual certification evidence and limits.
Assign recovery, disposal and documentation responsibilities.
Check state/local trade and permit questions.
Price technical escalation and backup cover before a response guarantee.

practicalOutput: HVAC equipment, task and technician matrix
limitations: No complete refrigerant-regime, technician, state-trade or permit determination.

title: A salon product standard needs a worker-exposure review
description: Investigate chemical handling and professional operation before requiring U.S. partners to use the home-market range.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A product claim is not the exposure assessment
paragraphs: OSHA explains that salon products containing or releasing formaldehyde can trigger formaldehyde and hazard-communication requirements. Its guidance describes assessment, protection and training steps. Historic product tests on the page are not evidence that any named product has the same formulation or status today.

sections.heading: Map the whole treatment process
paragraphs: Record actual products, safety data sheets, ingredients, heating/mixing steps, frequency, room layout, ventilation and worker roles. A bottle labelled formaldehyde-free is not the only evidence to examine. Use a competent assessment for actual conditions rather than substitute a brand’s quality checklist.

sections.heading: Professional and premises rules remain separate
paragraphs: Identify who employs staff and who may perform each service under the operating jurisdiction’s professional and establishment rules. This page does not research a particular state’s cosmetology permissions. Import and U.S. product-distribution responsibilities are additional workstreams if the brand supplies products.

sections.heading: Fictional product decision
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Singapore salon brand requires one smoothing treatment across its network. The U.S. operations lead compares the actual formulation and process with an alternative, recording worker protection, client specifications and training evidence before changing the approved list.

sections.heading: Prepare the product/process evidence sheet
paragraphs: Output: a treatment and worker-protection map owned by operations and safety.
bullets: Identify actual product and current safety information.
Record tasks and conditions that determine exposure.
Assign assessment, training and protective measures where applicable.
Separate state professional and establishment licensing questions.
Approve sourcing changes only after technical and compliance review.

practicalOutput: Salon treatment, chemical and worker-responsibility sheet
limitations: No product safety certification, exposure conclusion or state cosmetology authorisation.

title: Vehicle-service expansion needs a waste-stream operating plan
description: Identify used-oil roles and local environmental questions before a shop opens.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Used oil is an operating responsibility
paragraphs: EPA’s used-oil guidance points businesses to 40 CFR Part 279 and explains distinct generator, collection, transport and processing roles. It warns that state requirements can be stricter. A shop’s service-brand agreement does not settle what materials it handles or what environmental rules apply.

sections.heading: Separate the streams and the actors
paragraphs: Map lubricating oil, solvents, antifreeze, filters, batteries and other materials rather than call them all waste oil. Record who stores, collects, transports and receives each stream. Mixtures and disposal can change the analysis. A contractor invoice is evidence of a service, not blanket proof that the operator has satisfied every obligation.

sections.heading: Choose premises using the actual process
paragraphs: Record bays, containers, drainage, spill response, fire/building requirements and collection access as tasks for the appropriate authorities and competent reviewers. EPA describes good-condition, nonleaking container expectations in the cited guidance; other waste and state/local rules need their own evidence.

sections.heading: Fictional delivery question
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European quick-service brand investigates an existing U.S. workshop. Before adopting the home-market process, the operator maps where each material goes and obtains properly scoped handling and collection evidence. Unknown disposal, insurance and site-remediation costs stay unknown.

sections.heading: Prepare the waste-role worksheet
paragraphs: Output: a material/actor/evidence map owned by the shop operations lead.
bullets: Identify actual materials and their use/contamination history.
Assign handling role and applicable source for each stream.
Document containers, storage, spill and collection arrangements.
Check state environmental and local premises requirements.
Keep recommendations separate from legal duties and case-specific conclusions.

limitations: No particular waste classification, permit, cleanup or contractor approval.

title: Packaged-food expansion is a product and facility decision
description: Compare import, co-packing and U.S. production using the actual product and supply roles.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Define the product and facility first
paragraphs: FDA explains food-facility registration for covered manufacturing, processing, packing and holding, with specified exemptions. Its startup guide also distinguishes FDA and USDA product areas and state/local retail operation. A restaurant exemption cannot simply be assigned to a separate wholesale production facility.

sections.heading: Map who does each part of the supply chain
paragraphs: Record ingredients, process, packaging, facility location, label owner, importer and U.S. customer/channel. Importing finished goods, supplying a co-packer and licensing a manufacturing method can allocate different duties. Registration is not a statement that the product is approved.

sections.heading: Investigate the exact control pathway
paragraphs: Identify applicable product-specific rules, registration/exemption evidence, records, labels, preventive-control and import questions. This guide does not decide a particular commodity’s regulator, exemption or importer program. Put those issues ahead of supplier and territory commitments when they affect feasibility.

sections.heading: Fictional sourcing comparison
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Southeast Asian packaged-food brand compares importing one finished product with a U.S. co-packer. It records recipe tolerances, permitted label claims, minimum order, supplier lead time, quality control and product-specific legal responsibilities. A cheaper quote without that scope is an incomplete comparison.

sections.heading: Prepare the product/facility factsheet
paragraphs: Output: a supply-role and evidence map owned by the technical and supply leads.
bullets: Name actual product, ingredients and process.
Identify every facility and activity.
Record regulator and registration/exemption questions.
Assign label, importer, record and quality responsibilities.
Keep unknown tariffs, compliance costs and lead times visible.

practicalOutput: Product, facility and import/co-packing responsibility map
limitations: No product approval, import permission, exemption or comprehensive food-safety assessment.

title: Adding alcohol changes the entity, location and opening checklist
description: Separate federal dealer registration from state/local selling permission and other alcohol roles.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the actual seller before making promises
paragraphs: TTB’s retailer guidance describes federal dealer registration before the covered business begins, per-location treatment and records of receipts. It includes both on-site and off-site alcohol sales. Federal dealer registration is not a substitute for state or local authority to sell.

sections.heading: Keep the business roles distinct
paragraphs: A bar, restaurant or shop selling to consumers is not automatically authorised to import, produce or wholesale. Record the selling entity, premises, channel, supplier and whether the parent or partner takes title to products. Those facts affect the next regulatory workstream.

sections.heading: Put alcohol into the premises dependency plan
paragraphs: Before relying on alcohol revenue, investigate the actual state/local licence category, site suitability, ownership questions, approvals and timing. Landlord consent, a franchise agreement and a supplier commitment are separate documents. Do not assume that a licence transfers with an asset purchase or that home-country distribution rights carry across.

sections.heading: Fictional launch choice
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European restaurant brand expects wine sales in its first U.S. unit. The finance lead models an explicit no-alcohol opening scenario while the launch lead investigates the actual licensing path. This is a planning alternative, not a representation that a particular interim operation is permitted.

sections.heading: Prepare the alcohol-role worksheet
paragraphs: Output: a seller/location/permission matrix owned by the launch lead.
bullets: Name the entity selling each product and each location/channel.
Record applicable federal dealer registration and receipt evidence.
Investigate state/local licence and ownership requirements.
Separate importing, production and wholesale questions.
Tie revenue assumptions to actual permission and opening dependencies.

practicalOutput: Alcohol selling-entity, location and evidence matrix
limitations: No alcohol licence, import permit, product approval or permission to open.
